subject: Physics
prompt: Direction of angular velocity vector (right-hand rule)
explain: ω is an axial vector; direction given by right-hand screw rule along rotation axis.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pseudo force experienced in rotating frame (centrifugal)
explain: In rotating frame, centrifugal pseudo force = mω²r directed radially outward.

subject: Physics
prompt: In non-uniform circular motion, net acceleration direction
explain: Non-uniform UCM has both centripetal (radial) and tangential components of acceleration.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle swept by radius vector is called?
explain: Angular displacement θ is the angle swept by the radius vector in circular motion.

subject: Physics
prompt: Banking angle θ for max safe speed with friction μ on banked road?
explain: Max speed uses friction up the slope: v_max² = rg·tan(θ+φ), φ=arctan(μ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Conical pendulum: horizontal component of tension provides?
explain: T·sinθ acts horizontally toward axis, providing the centripetal force mω²r.

subject: Physics
prompt: In uniform circular motion, angular momentum is?
explain: No tangential force → no torque → angular momentum remains constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: For non-uniform circular motion, tangential force is responsible for?
explain: Tangential force changes the magnitude of velocity (speed), not its direction.

subject: Physics
prompt: Kinetic energy of particle in uniform circular motion is?
explain: Speed is constant in UCM, so KE = ½mv² remains constant throughout.

subject: Physics
prompt: Overturning condition for vehicle on flat curve (track width 2d, height h)?
explain: Outer wheel lifts when mv²h/r ≥ mgd, i.e., v² ≥ gd·r/h (for fixed r, d, h).

subject: Physics
prompt: In a rotating frame, centrifugal force on mass m is directed?
explain: Centrifugal (pseudo) force = mω²r acts radially outward in rotating frame.

subject: Physics
prompt: Difference between angular speed of hour and minute hand of clock?

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between linear velocity v and angular velocity ω in vector form?
explain: v = ω × r; using right-hand rule gives direction tangent to circular path.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle between net acceleration and radius in non-uniform circular motion?
explain: aₜ is perpendicular to ac (radius); angle from radius = tan⁻¹(aₜ/ac).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a banked road, what happens if speed < optimum speed (with friction)?
explain: Below optimum speed, friction acts up the slope preventing inward skidding; car tends to skid inward.

subject: Physics
prompt: The centripetal force on a satellite in circular orbit is provided by?
explain: Gravitational attraction between satellite and Earth provides the centripetal force for orbital motion.

subject: Physics
prompt: If T is time period, angular displacement in T/4 is?
explain: In full period T, displacement = 2π. In T/4, displacement = 2π/4 = π/2 rad.

subject: Physics
prompt: Radial (centripetal) acceleration is also called?
explain: Centripetal acceleration points toward center along the radius; it is also called normal acceleration.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle in UCM: its velocity vector rotates by angle Δθ in Δt. |Δv| equals?
explain: For small Δθ, |Δv| = vΔθ (chord of velocity hodograph), confirming aᶜ = v·(dθ/dt) = v²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between angular quantities: ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ is analogous to?
explain: Third equation of rotational kinematics mirrors v² = u² + 2as from linear motion.

subject: Physics
prompt: Distance travelled by a particle in one complete revolution (radius r)?
explain: Circumference of the circle = 2πr; this is the path length per revolution.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between linear speed v, radius r, and time period T?
explain: In one period T, particle travels circumference 2πr, so speed v = 2πr/T.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal acceleration of Earth in its orbit: which pair correctly describes it?
explain: Earth's centripetal acceleration points toward Sun (centre of orbit) and is very small (~0.006 m/s²).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a vehicle on a curved road, overturning tendency increases if centre of gravity is?
explain: Higher CG increases the overturning torque due to centrifugal force, making overturning easier.

subject: Physics
prompt: In non-uniform circular motion, what is the angle between net acceleration and centripetal acceleration?
explain: Net acceleration has radial (aᶜ) and tangential (aₜ) components; angle with radius = tan⁻¹(aₜ/aᶜ).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a particle on outside of a circular track (top), condition to leave the track?
explain: On outside at top, mg − N = mv²/r; leaves track (N = 0) when v = √(gr); leaves if v > √(gr).

subject: Physics
prompt: A ball in vertical circle: at what angle from bottom is speed equal to √(gr)?
explain: Speed at any point depends on initial speed at bottom; no universal angle for v=√(gr).

subject: Physics
prompt: A car rounds a curve. Which force is the reaction pair of friction on car from road?
explain: By Newton's third law, friction on car from road is paired with friction on road from car.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle in UCM: magnitude of change in velocity vector over quarter revolution (speed v) is?
explain: Vectors at 90° to each other: |Δv| = √(v²+v²) = v√2.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a vehicle on banked road, normal force N compared to mg is?
explain: N cosθ = mg ⟹ N = mg/cosθ > mg since cosθ < 1 for θ > 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: For circular motion, which rotational kinematic equation relates θ, ω₀, α, t?
explain: Analogous to s = ut + ½at², angular version uses θ, ω₀, α, t.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a particle on OUTSIDE of top of circular track, it leaves track when?
explain: Normal force = 0 at leave point: mg − N = mv²/r, so N=0 gives v²=gr; leaves if v²≥gr.

subject: Physics
prompt: A pendulum bob moves in a horizontal circle. Its time period is independent of?
explain: Time period of conical pendulum T = 2π√(Lcosθ/g) is independent of mass.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle moves in circle of radius r. The ratio of distance to displacement after 3/4 revolution is?
explain: Distance = (3/4)×2πr = 3πr/2; displacement = r√2; ratio = 3πr/2 ÷ r√2 = 3π/(2√2).

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal acceleration in terms of v and T (time period)?
explain: Since v = 2πr/T, a = v²/r = v·(2π/T).

subject: Physics
prompt: In UCM, if radius triples keeping speed same, time period T changes by factor?
explain: T = 2πr/v; with v constant, T ∝ r, so T triples.

subject: Physics
prompt: For circular motion, which equation is analogous to v² = u² + 2as?
explain: Rotational kinematics mirrors linear: ω²=ω₀²+2αθ corresponds to v²=u²+2as.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle on inside top of circular loop leaves track when speed v satisfies?
explain: At top, N + mg = mv²/r; N=0 gives v=√(gr); below this speed contact is lost.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car of mass m on flat road takes a turn of radius r. Friction force required is?
explain: On flat road, friction alone provides centripetal force f = mv²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: For conical pendulum, angular speed ω in terms of g and vertical height h (= L cosθ)?
explain: h = L cosθ; from T cosθ = mg and T sinθ = mω²r, ω² = g/h.

subject: Physics
prompt: Dimension of centripetal acceleration?
explain: Centripetal acceleration has dimensions of acceleration: LT⁻².

subject: Physics
prompt: In uniform circular motion, what is the angle between Δv and the velocity v?
explain: Δv (centripetal direction) points toward centre, perpendicular to velocity v (tangential).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a vehicle rounding a curve, overturning occurs BEFORE skidding when?
explain: Overturning condition (h/d > μ) is satisfied first when the CG is high relative to track width.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a conical pendulum, time period T = 2π√(L cosθ/g). If θ increases, T?
explain: As θ increases, cosθ decreases, so T = 2π√(Lcosθ/g) decreases.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a body in circular motion, angular momentum L about centre when radius doubles (same ω)?
explain: L = mωr²; if r doubles (same ω), L ∝ r², so L becomes 4L.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal force on a satellite is gravitational. If orbital radius doubles, centripetal force?
explain: Gravitational force ∝ 1/r²; doubling r reduces F by factor 4.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle completes one revolution in time T. Its average velocity over T/2 is?
explain: In T/2, displacement = diameter = 2r; average velocity = 2r/(T/2) = 4r/T... wait: displacement=2r, time=T/2, so avg v=2r÷(T/2)=4r/T.

subject: Physics
prompt: In uniform circular motion, average acceleration over a full time period T is?
explain: After one full revolution, Δv = 0 (velocity returns to same vector), so average acceleration = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle in UCM: ratio of angular speed to frequency (ω/f)?
explain: By definition ω = 2πf, so ω/f = 2π.

subject: Physics
prompt: On banked road (no friction), normal force N equals?
explain: Vertical equilibrium: N cosθ = mg → N = mg/cosθ.

subject: Physics
prompt: A stone whirled in vertical circle. When string is horizontal, centripetal force is provided by?
explain: When string is horizontal, tension is purely radial (centripetal); mg acts downward (tangential).

subject: Physics
prompt: In circular motion with constant speed, tangential acceleration aₜ = ?
explain: Constant speed means no tangential acceleration; only centripetal (radial) acceleration exists.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle moves in a vertical circle. The speed is maximum at the?
explain: By energy conservation, speed is maximum at the lowest point where PE is minimum.

subject: Physics
prompt: For circular motion, torque of centripetal force about the centre of circle is?
explain: Centripetal force is along radius (toward centre); torque = r × F = 0 as they are antiparallel.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a vertical circle (bead on wire), at topmost point centripetal force = mg + N. If N = 0, speed v = ?
explain: At top for bead on wire: mg + N = mv²/r; N=0 gives v = √(gr). (String needs 5gr at bottom.)
